newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle bid $62, passed - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle bid $62, passed - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle bids early Tuesday were light at $62.00 per cwt, unchanged from last week's top and passed by owners pricing cattle at $64.00 to $65.00, feedlot sources said.
"Phone call activity has picked up but not enough to indicate there will be any trade," a Texas Panhandle-area feedlot manager said.
Owners were looking for higher cattle prices this week amid strong CME live cattle futures and perceptions that beef prices were poised to rebound, cattle feeders said.
Outlooks for fewer market-ready cattle within the next few weeks fortified owners' resolve for higher prices.

"If $63.00 (bids) come today, I don't think we'll see many trade because most people will sit back a minute and wait looking for $64.00, which is not out of the realm of possibility," a Kansas feedlot operator said.
Whatever the trade level, volume is going to be important, sources said.

Most feedlots have been able to stay current while marketing large numbers of cattle so far this summer. If feedlots can remain current, it opens the door to higher prices as supplies start coming down in the weeks ahead, they said.
